about.title: Carson Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Carson sits where the 405 and the 91 cross paths, and the traffic that funnels through it shapes the collision picture. Public records for 2025 list 383 injury collisions inside city limits, with 507 people hurt and two lives lost. The corridors that show up most often are the San Diego Freeway, the Artesia Freeway, Avalon Boulevard and Carson Street, and reports cluster on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 as commuters head home. Behind each number is someone dealing with pain, missed shifts and an adjuster who calls before the tow bill even arrives. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that pairs you with an independent California attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless money is recovered. California gives you two years to file in most cases, but evidence from a freeway crash disappears far sooner than that. A quick conversation now protects your options later, and it costs you nothing to ask.

whyChoose.title: Why Carson Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than They Look
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a public agency such as Caltrans or the city is involved. The attorney you are matched with can flag that early, before a claim quietly expires.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Does Not Shut the Door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you carried some of the blame; your share simply reduces the amount. An attorney will push back on inflated fault percentages the other insurer may assign to you.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, and our matching service is free. You pay nothing up front, and nothing at all if the case does not produce a recovery.

items.question: My crash happened on the 405 in Carson. Does it matter that it was a state freeway?
items.answer: It can. If a road condition, missing signage or a construction zone played a role, a government entity such as Caltrans might share responsibility, and claims against public agencies in California often must be filed within six months rather than two years. Even in an ordinary two-car collision, freeway crashes frequently involve multiple vehicles and competing accounts, so gathering dashcam footage, witness contacts and the CHP report quickly matters. An attorney can sort out who to pursue and on what timeline.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize your injuries or shift fault onto you. Stick to reporting the crash to your own carrier as your policy requires, and let a lawyer handle communication with the other side.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in California?
items.answer: For most car accident cases, no. California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, emotional distress or loss of enjoyment of life in ordinary auto injury claims. The value depends on the specifics of your injuries, your recovery and how the case is documented, which is why preserving medical records and photos from the start is so important.
